methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - roanoke.edu
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab signals grassroots capability-building outside major metros, suggesting peer-to-peer knowledge transfer could distribute AI fluency beyond NoVA's gravity well if scaled across similar institutions.

signals.title: Fairfax City Business Leaders Tell Spanberger About Rising Costs, AI, Workforce Challenges - patch.com
signals.signal_reading: Business leaders discussing AI challenges with Congressional representatives reveals AI adoption concentrated in NoVA's business ecosystem, where proximity to capital and workforce creates self-reinforcing advantages unavailable to rural regions.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests platform-delivered tools are creating broad but shallow adoption patterns in secondary metros, where workers must adapt quickly without deep technical training infrastructure.

signals.title: Learning Law in the AI Age - University of Virginia School of Law
signals.source: University of Virginia School of Law
signals.signal_reading: UVA Law School integrating AI into legal education deepens capability at elite institutions, but this professional-track adoption concentrates expertise in credentialed pathways inaccessible to most Virginians outside university ecosystems.

signals.title: Meta kicks off program in Richmond to give free AI glasses to every legally blind veteran in the US - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Meta distributing AI glasses to veterans through Richmond signals platform companies delivering turnkey AI tools that enable broad access without requiring deep technical knowledge, democratizing capability through consumer products rather than skills development.
